chunks: Muḥammad ibn Muslim narrated from him, عليه السلام, that he said:
"When you fast, then let your hearing, your sight, your hair, and your skin fast as well," and he mentioned other things besides this.
And he said: "The day of your fasting should not be like the day of your breaking the fast."

key_terms.بَصَرُكَ: your sight; what one looks at during the fast
key_terms.جِلْدُكَ: your skin; the body as participating in fasting discipline
key_terms.سَمْعُكَ: your hearing; what one listens to during the fast
key_terms.فَلْيَصُمْ: then let it fast; a command for restraint during sawm (fasting)
key_terms.فِطْرِكَ: your breaking of the fast; the non-fasting state

ai.seo_question: How should a believer’s senses and behavior fast during the day of sawm (fasting)?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that fasting is not limited to refraining from food and drink, but includes moral restraint of the senses and the body. It emphasizes the etiquette of sawm (fasting), so that a fasting day is spiritually distinct from an ordinary day.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1855 - Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Imam (as) that Imam (as) said:
"When you fast, let your hearing, your sight, your hair, and your skin also fast," and Imam mentioned other things besides these.
Imam (as) also said: "The day of your fast should not be like the day when you are not fasting."
